book-of-kells.title: Book of Kells, folio 292r (incipit to the Gospel of John)
book-of-kells.location: Trinity College Library, Dublin (the manuscript's own likely origin is Iona or a related Columban monastery, Scotland/Ireland)
book-of-kells.story: An actual page from an actual illuminated Gospel manuscript, not a modern recreation - the opening words of John's Gospel ("In principio erat Verbum") transformed into an ornamental icon of its own, exactly the kind of devotional artistry the monastic scriptoria of the early medieval West produced. Stands for the Church's first several centuries as a manuscript-and-monastery culture, before print.
book-of-kells.author: Unknown (the manuscript's own medieval illuminator; photographic reproduction author not recorded on the file page)
book-of-kells.date_taken: unspecified (photographic reproduction of a manuscript created c. 800 CE)
book-of-kells.attribution: Public domain (faithful photographic reproduction of a public-domain manuscript page), via Wikimedia Commons

chartres-cathedral.title: Chartres Cathedral (Notre-Dame de Chartres), exterior
chartres-cathedral.period: High Gothic, c. 1194-1250 (the present cathedral, rebuilt after the 1194 fire; largely complete by c. 1220)
chartres-cathedral.story: One of the best-preserved and most complete of the great High Gothic cathedrals, still standing largely as built - a real, physical monument to the Church's own high-medieval building projects, its cult of the Virgin, and its cathedral schools.

hagia-sophia-mosaic.title: Christ Pantocrator, the Deesis mosaic, Hagia Sophia
hagia-sophia-mosaic.period: c. 1261 CE (the Deesis mosaic is generally dated to the restoration following the Byzantine recovery of Constantinople from Latin Crusader rule)
hagia-sophia-mosaic.story: One of the finest surviving works of Byzantine mosaic art, from the church that was Eastern Christianity's own imperial cathedral for nearly a thousand years - fills a real gap in the set: nothing else here represents the Byzantine/Eastern Orthodox tradition or the Great Schism's own world. HONEST CAVEAT: Hagia Sophia was reconverted from a museum back into an active mosque in 2020; the mosaic is not permanently hidden, but it is now periodically covered with curtains during prayer times - the building's current religious use is a live, contested question, not a settled museum-piece past.

gutenberg-bible.title: Gutenberg Bible, Lenox copy (New York Public Library)
gutenberg-bible.location: New York Public Library, USA (one of c. 49 surviving copies/partial copies of Johannes Gutenberg's 42-line Bible, printed in Mainz)
gutenberg-bible.story: The printing press as its own turning point in the Church's story - arguably more consequential for everything that follows (mass-produced vernacular Scripture, the Reformation's own pamphlet wars, the modern missionary movement's printed literature) than any single hand-copied manuscript, however beautiful. This is a real photograph of a real surviving copy, not a stock rendering.

wittenberg-theses-door.title: The Theses Door, Schlosskirche (Castle Church), Wittenberg
wittenberg-theses-door.period: Event date 1517 (Luther's traditional posting of the Ninety-Five Theses)
wittenberg-theses-door.story: The physical site of the traditional starting point of the Reformation. HONEST CAVEAT, already flagged in the sourcing brief and confirmed here: the visible bronze doors are an 1858 commemorative recasting (with the Theses text cast directly into the bronze), not the original 1517 wooden door, which burned in an 18th-century fire. The site and the tradition are genuine; the door itself is a 19th-century monument to the event, not a surviving artifact of it.

mother-bethel-ame.title: Mother Bethel A.M.E. Church
mother-bethel-ame.period: Congregation founded 1794 (the oldest African Methodist Episcopal congregation in the nation); present building completed 1890
mother-bethel-ame.story: The American story of Black Christian faith and self-determination under and after slavery: founded by Richard Allen and others who walked out of St. George's Methodist Church in 1792 over segregated worship, on the oldest parcel of land in the United States continuously owned by African Americans. HONEST CAVEAT, matching this project's own established standard for this kind of site: the visible building is the fourth structure on this ground, completed in 1890 - not the original 1794 church, which was a converted blacksmith's shop. The continuity is institutional and the land itself, not the standing fabric.

yamoussoukro-basilica.title: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace (Notre-Dame de la Paix)
yamoussoukro-basilica.story: One of the largest churches in the world, built at the initiative of Côte d'Ivoire's first president, Félix Houphouët-Boigny, on the model of St. Peter's Basilica - a genuine, monumental "global church, Global South" building, standing for the twentieth century's real shift of Christianity's own numerical and institutional center of gravity toward Africa.
